LESSON: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – PLAYS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays, part of Strand 5 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do you read for information? 2. How can plays be used to preserve our cultural heritage?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to read plays related to the theme,

2. work collaboratively to identify vocabulary related to the theme from the plays,

3. list the vocabulary on flashcards and organise them in a vocabulary bank,

4. use the vocabulary to fill word puzzles,

5. work with peers to construct simple paragraphs,

6. answer direct and inferential questions on the play read,

7. work collaboratively to discuss the lessons learnt from the plays read and make connections to real life,

8. roleplay one of the plays read with peers in class,

9. work with peers to record the play and store the recorded clip in a digital portfolio. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to read plays related to the theme,
2. work collaboratively to identify vocabulary related to the theme from the plays,
3. list the vocabulary on flashcards and organise them in a vocabulary bank,
4. use the vocabulary to fill word puzzles,
5. work with peers to construct simple paragraphs,
6. answer direct and inferential questions on the play read,
7. work collaboratively to discuss the lessons learnt from the plays read and make connections to real life,
8. roleplay one of the plays read with peers in class,
9. work with peers to record the play and store the recorded clip in a digital portfolio. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information – Plays together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem-solving. This is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts by logical reasoning when using

the vocabulary to fill word puzzles.

• Digital Literacy: It is promoted as the learner uses digital technology to record the play and store the recorded clip in a

digital portfolio.

Values:
• Social Justice: It is enhanced as the learner accords equal opportunities in sharing roles when roleplaying one of the plays

read with peers in class.

• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner displays patience when conducting a reader’s theatre to read plays related to the

theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural Awareness: This is enhanced as the learner reads texts on cultural heritage and role-plays with peers in class on the

theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the vocabulary derived from plays on cultural heritage to concepts on the social organisation of

communities in Social Studies.
